question: What does the permit-limit comment 'WHEN DISCHARGING' do to monitoring/limit applicability?

judgment.semantic_question_used: Does the permit limit comment 'WHEN DISCHARGING.' establish that weekly grab pH maximum monitoring (≤9.0 standard units) for backwash water discharge is required only when discharge occurs, rather than unconditionally each reporting period?
judgment.interpretation: The DMR_COMMENT_TEXT 'WHEN DISCHARGING.' implements permit footnote *1 for Outfall 001 backwash water limits. For this permit limit row (pH maximum 9.0 standard units, grab sample, monthly DMR reporting frequency code 01/07), monitoring and limit applicability are conditioned on actual discharge: the permittee must monitor pH weekly by grab sample only during periods when backwash discharge occurs. Monitoring is not required for weeks or months with no discharge from the outfall.
judgment.grounding: Permit NM0028762 Part I discharge limitations table lists pH (STORET 00400) with minimum 6.6, maximum 9.0, monitoring frequency '1/Week (*1)', sample type Grab, and footnote '*1 When discharging.' The structured permit_limits.csv row for limit_value_id 3610840345 carries DMR_COMMENT_TEXT 'WHEN DISCHARGING.' on the DISCHARGE BACKWASH WATER limit set matching that outfall. The statement of basis states 'pH shall continue to be monitored weekly when discharging' and describes intermittent filter backwash discharge (roughly daily to every three to four days seasonally). No-discharge months are reported by marking the NO DISCHARGE box on the DMR; FY2025 DMR rows for this limit_value_id report numeric pH values with empty NODI_CODE for every month October 2024 through September 2025, consistent with discharge-period monitoring rather than documented no-discharge periods.

snippets.text: pH shall continue to be monitored weekly when discharging.
Filter backwash using potable water occurs from once per day to once every three to four days depending on the plant and the time of year.
If there is no discharge from any outfall during the sampling month, place an "X" in the NO DISCHARGE box located in the upper right corner of the Discharge Monitoring Report.

judgment.remaining_uncertainty: The comment semantics are resolved, but structured sources alone do not provide a dedicated per-period discharge-occurrence field. For any specific FY2025 monitoring period, whether the conditional monitoring obligation was triggered must be inferred from DMR no-discharge reporting, flow evidence, or other discharge documentation rather than from the comment text itself. This occurrence row does not by itself establish discharge status for sibling parameters or limit rows.
